newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CAPELLO LOOKS FOR WIN OVER BARCELONA TO PLACATE FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAPELLO LOOKS FOR WIN OVER BARCELONA TO PLACATE FANS.

text.p: Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello hopes to placate fans angered by his impending departure by securing a win at Barcelona on Saturday to all but guarantee Real's 27th Spanish championship.

Real, eight points ahead in the championship, have not won a league match at Barcelona in 13 seasons and a draw would be a good result for the visitors but Capello is adamant: "We never go out to draw."

Part of the wrath surrounding the announcement of Capello's decision to leave came from the rumour that the former AC Milan man had been negotiating to move to Barcelona, an act tantamount to sacrilege in the eyes of Real fans.
Capello has not yet revealed his plans but most signs point against his going to Barcelona. Instead Capello is expected to return to struggling Italian champions Milan.
Capello's opposite number Bobby Robson is hoping that a win over the old enemy on Saturday would boost his side's faith in him as coach.
Since joining the club in the close season, the former England manager has struggled to convince fans, the media and -- so the rumours go -- even the players, of his capabilities.
The latest speculation points to Robson's staying on in a different position, leaving the hot seat in the Camp Nou to somebody else, possibly Ajax's Louis Van Gaal.
The future of several Barcelona players is also in doubt.
Strikers Ronaldo and Luis Figo and midfielders Gheorghe Popescu and Josep Guardiola are all reported to have received offers from Italian clubs and possibly from Real as well.
Barcelona president Jose Luis Nunez said earlier this week that he would not talk about the future of the players until after the big match.
But Nunez did take the opportunity to sow discord in the enemy camp by saying that four Real players had offered themselves to Barcelona as possible signings.
"They could score a few goals...two of them are forwards," said Nunez, in what Spanish commentators saw as a clear reference to Real's Balkan strike force of Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic.
Both players are known to be unhappy after being repeatedly substituted by Capello.
Capello has unexpectedly called midfielder Victor Sanchez back from exile in the reserves for Saturday's match.

The reappearance of the 20-year-old Sanchez, who excelled in December's 2-0 win over Barcelona but had struggled to impress since, is likely to leave troubled former international Emilio Amavisca on the bench.
Robson has left out French central defender Laurent Blanc, who is still recovering from injury, and off-form Nigerian winger Emmanuel Amunike.
